LESSON: FISHING IN EASTERN AFRICA

Grade: Grade 6
Subject: SOCIAL STUDIES
Strand: RESOURCES AND ECONOMIC ACTIVITIES IN EASTERN AFRICA Strand Sub- Strand Specific 
Topic 3.2: Fishing in Eastern Africa
Suggested lessons in curriculum: 5

SECTION 1: INTRODUCTION

This lesson covers Fishing in Eastern Africa, part of RESOURCES AND ECONOMIC ACTIVITIES IN EASTERN AFRICA Strand Sub- Strand Specific  in Grade 6 SOCIAL STUDIES.

Key inquiry question: Why is fishing important to the Eastern Africa communitie s?

You will study the official KICD learning outcomes, classroom activities, values, and competencies for this topic. Use Kenyan examples from your county, school, and community throughout.

SECTION 2: LEARNING OUTCOMES

By the end of this topic, you should be able to:

A. locate marine and inland fishing grounds on a map,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fishing in Eastern Africa in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

B. describe methods of marine fishing in Eastern Africa,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fishing in Eastern Africa in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

C. explain challenges facing fishing in Eastern Africa,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fishing in Eastern Africa in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

D. design possible solutions to challenges facing fishing in Eastern Africa,

   Learning focus: This outcome is part of Fishing in Eastern Africa in the Kenya CBC curriculum.
   In class: Your teacher will guide you to discuss, practise, and demonstrate this skill using examples from Kenya.
   At home: Explain this point to a parent using an example from your school, home, or community.

E. value fishing as an economic activity. Learner is guided to: ● locate on a map the marine and inland fishing grounds in Eastern Africa, ● discuss the methods of marine fishing in Eastern Africa and present in class, ● use digital devices/print resources to research methods of marine fishing in Eastern Africa, ● brainstorm on the challenges facing marine fishing in Eastern Africa. ● engage a fisheries officer to identify possible solutions to challenges facing marine fishing in Eastern Africa. F. Suggested learning experiences (from KICD)

1. brainstorm on factors that promote tourism in Eastern Africa,

2. draw a map of Eastern Africa and locate game reserves and national parks,

3. engage a Game Ranger on possible solutions to the challenges facing tourism in Eastern Africa,

4. design posters and charts on challenges and solutions facing tourism,

5. participate in conservation of wildlife walk/run activities in the locality.

SECTION 4: LEARNING ACTIVITIES

A. At school

1. brainstorm on factors that promote tourism in Eastern Africa,
2. draw a map of Eastern Africa and locate game reserves and national parks,
3. engage a Game Ranger on possible solutions to the challenges facing tourism in Eastern Africa,
4. design posters and charts on challenges and solutions facing tourism,
5. participate in conservation of wildlife walk/run activities in the locality.

B. At home with your parent or guardian

1. Read this lesson on Fishing in Eastern Africa together.
2. Discuss the key inquiry question and give examples from your area.
3. Write five sentences summarising what you learned.
4. Prepare for the revision quiz at the end of this topic.

SECTION 5: CORE COMPETENCIES, VALUES, AND PCIs

Core Competencies to be developed:
● Communication and collaboration: Learners listen critically as they discuss challenges facing marine fishing.

● Learning to learn: Learners work collaboratively as they engage with a fisheries officer to identify possible solutions to

challenges facing marine fishing in Eastern Africa.

Values:
Unity: Learners collaborate with others as they discuss and write down possible solutions to challenges facing marine fishing

in Eastern Africa.

● Responsibility: Learners proactively solve problems as they illustrate methods of marine fishing in Eastern Africa using

appropriate media.

Pertinent and Contemporary Issues:
(PCIs):

Critical thinking skills: Learners discuss, in groups, and write down possible solutions to challenges facing marine fishing

in Eastern Africa.

Link to Other Learning Areas:

● Learners use Pre-technical Studies knowledge to discuss the methods of marine fishing in Eastern Africa.

● Learners use Mathematics knowledge to locate on a map the main fishing grounds in Eastern Africa.
